title: Uniform continuity on an interval restricts to any sub-interval with the SAME modulus
statement: If F is CReal.UniformlyContinuousOn [a,b], and a<=a'<=b'<=b, then F is CReal.UniformlyContinuousOn [a',b'] -- using the identical modulus witness, no new estimate. UniformlyContinuousOn's own spec only ever uses its range hypotheses (a<=x, x<=b, a<=y, y<=b) to state the closeness implication, and a<=a'<=x together with y<=b'<=b compose to exactly those via CReal.le_trans. Built directly against the witness constructor rather than through the recursor: the new spec is a lambda wrapping the ORIGINAL witness's own spec applied to the composed range proofs, so UniformlyContinuousOn's definition is never unfolded.

formal.statement: theorem CReal.uniformlyContinuousOn_restrict : ((x0 : ((x0 : CReal) -> CReal)) -> ((x1 : CReal) -> ((x2 : CReal) -> ((x3 : CReal) -> ((x4 : CReal) -> ((x5 : CReal.UniformlyContinuousOn x0 x1 x2) -> ((x6 : CReal.le x1 x3) -> ((x7 : CReal.le x3 x4) -> ((x8 : CReal.le x4 x2) -> CReal.UniformlyContinuousOn x0 x3 x4)))))))))
